discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant (Z2) topological insulators
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary band insulator into a new state of matter, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 topological invariant and protected by time-reversal symmetry, with helical edge states immune to backscattering. Their simple, transparent model made a sharp prediction and introduced the topological classification of band insulators. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed the quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, the first experimental topological insulator, which turned an abstract Berry-curvature concept into a measurable, controllable phenomenon. Theory and experiment advanced together. The discovery launched three-dimensional topological insulators, topological superconductivity, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and the classification of topological materials. It reshaped condensed-matter physics and materials science, and it set the agenda for thousands of groups worldwide.
